comments.author: @mshonle
comments.text: It seems off to use a raw web DOM (after all JS on the page executes) as the baseline for a processing task. The LLMs in comparison were mostly trained on text, not DOM, so it’d be natural for their tokenizers to be suboptimal at it. A better basis of comparison would be the accessibility-processed DOM (for example, the output that would go to Braille or audio output for the visually impaired).

comments.author: @GregoryMcCarthy123
comments.text: I want to start off saying this seems pretty cool, although maybe it’s just an SBC running a multimodal LLM like LLAVA wrapped in cute shiny components. It’s not immediately clear how / why they would host the user’s interactions on their own cloud, using their own servers and resources if there is no subscription. Something doesn’t quite add up. It could be the case that they believe their model is so unique they worry about it being reverse engineered, in which case keeping such work hidden behind a VM makes sense. It would be cool to get some open source stuff that allows you to easily train “tasks” and then have local LLMs execute them. I believe this is the reasoning for hosting the task execution on their private cloud.

comments.author: @glowing_kitty
comments.text: Some of the aspecs of the hardware are certainly interesting and promising (assuming the demo was real). But I also find it amusing how at the same time the scenarios they show are so far away from reality. Never in my life have I seen anyone using voice control / voice assistants outside of home or cars. Using them outside while walking, in public transport, in public places / restaurants and so on is just completely annoying to other people around you. Also, there is a reason why Voice assistants and voice controlled devices are not the standard way of interacting with electronics. There are only few scenarios where they are clearly the better way to interact with a device. In basically all other scenarios text input or touch / mouse / eye control is way more practical in real life. Voice input should be one of the input options, not the primary input option.
